test_title: PYST 51: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following schemes adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach to reap the benefit of scale in terms of procurement of inputs, availing common services and marketing of products?

options.text: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
Production Linked Incentive Scheme For Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI)
Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As part of the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, the Ministry of Food Processing **Industries has introduced the **"PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme,"** a centrally sponsored initiative spanning across India.
 
• This scheme aims to provide financial, technical, and business assistance for the enhancement of existing micro food processing enterprises.
 
• The PMFME Scheme implements the One District One Product (ODOP) approach, leveraging the advantages of scale in procurement of inputs, access to common services, and marketing of products.
 
• Each district focuses on a specific product under the ODOP framework, facilitating value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure.
 
• It's noteworthy that a district may feature more than one cluster of ODOP products, or a cluster may encompass multiple adjacent districts.
 
• The Ministry has already sanctioned ODOP for 707 districts across 35 States/Union Territories, encompassing a total of 137 unique products.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• In 2016, the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)** proposed an integrated program aimed at fostering the development of agro-marine processing and agro-processing clusters or estates. This initiative was allocated a budget of Rs 6,000 crore for the period spanning 2016 to 2020.
 
• The government has given its nod to the new guidelines for the **Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)**. These guidelines are set to be implemented during the 15th Finance Commission Cycle, spanning from 2021-22 to 2025-26.
 
• The Cabinet, in one of its meetings, has approved the Central Sector Scheme known as the **“Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI).” **This scheme is designed to bolster the creation of global food manufacturing champions that align with India’s natural resource endowment. Additionally, it aims to bolster Indian brands of food products in international markets. The scheme comes with an impressive outlay of Rs.10900 crore.
